text.p: Heavily indebted Finnish passenger ferry operator Silja Oy said in a statement on Thursday it proposes to redeem outstanding debentures and issue new shares to lift its equity to assets ratio.

"The strengthening of the capital structure and of the equity to assets ratio will be implemented so that the company will launch a share issue targeted at the public, and will offer to redeem its convertible debenture loans," Silja said.

Its seven biggest owners, Sweden's NCC, and Finnish UPM-Kymmene, Enso, Pohjola, Neste, Teollisuusvakuutus and Merita had pledged to sell debentures for 325 million markka, and to subscribe shares "for at least the corresponding amount," Silja said.
Silja issued two convertible debenture loans in 1994 and 1995, one worth 330 million markka and the other 353 million markka.

It now offered to redeem these debentures at 92.1555 percent -- up 25 percent on the price of the paper on the Helsinki Stock Exchange. The new shares will be issued at 39.50 markka each, also 25 percent higher than the share price on the bourse, it said.
At 1555, Silja's A share traded at 33.00 markka, 1.50 markka up on Wednesday's close.

Provided that the share issue was subscribed in full, the number of Silja shares in circulation could increase by 23 million from 13.5 million currently. Silja shares carry a nominal value of 20.00 markka each.
"The share issue is dimensioned in such a way that all holders of debentures and current shareholders will have the possibility to subscribe shares," Silja said.

A senior Silja official told Reuters by telephone that an increase of 23 million shares was "a theoretical maximum if absolutely every one of our small shareholders also use the opportunity to subscribe to not see their holding diluted."
Silja said it will not be able to convert the debentures it redeems into shares.
"Through the proposed measures, the company's debts will decrease by at least 310 million markka and the equity-to-assets ratio will rise by at least six percentage points," Silja said.
At end-September, Silja's long-term liabilities were 3.16 billion markka and its equity ratio was 10.5 percent.
The proposed measures will be put before an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on December 4.
